issues.legal_issue: A loss on the sale of depreciable business assets may be allowed when the business was carried on during only part of the accounting year.
material_facts: The assessee operated the colliery until the sale agreement was made during the accounting year, a finding of fact by the Tribunal that was not challenged.
Machinery and plant had been used for the colliery business and were sold during the accounting year.
The written-down value of the sold assets exceeded the sale amount, and the resulting loss was written off in the assessee’s books.
issues.conclusion: The loss was allowable in computing the assessee’s total income; the business and assets did not need to be used for the whole accounting year.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 10(2)(vii) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, the excess of the written-down value of sold buildings, machinery or plant over the sale amount is allowable where the amount is written off in the assessee’s books. The Court followed Commissioner of Income Tax, Bombay City II v. National Syndicate, which held that neither the business nor the use of the assets had to continue for the whole accounting year.

rule.if: tax_assessment_appeal and business_operated_part_year and depreciable_business_assets_used and depreciable_business_assets_sold_during_year and written_down_value_exceeded_sale_amount and loss_written_off_in_books

predicates.tax_assessment_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning the assessment of taxable income.
predicates.business_operated_part_year: The taxpayer carried on the business during part of the relevant accounting year.
predicates.depreciable_business_assets_used: The taxpayer used the depreciable assets in carrying on the business.
predicates.depreciable_business_assets_sold_during_: The taxpayer sold the depreciable assets during the relevant accounting year.
predicates.written_down_value_exceeded_sale_amount: The written-down value of the sold assets exceeded the amount received for them.
predicates.loss_written_off_in_books: The taxpayer wrote off the resulting loss in its books.

issues.definition: When an assessment appeal concerns a business operated during part of the year and used depreciable assets that were sold during that year for less than their written-down value, the loss is allowable if it was written off in the taxpayer’s books.

issues.legal_issue: Dividends from shares held as trading stock may be set off against brought-forward business losses when the taxpayer carried on business during part of the relevant year.
material_facts: The assessee carried on the colliery business during part of the relevant assessment year.
The assessee received dividends on shares during that year.
The shares formed part of the stock-in-trade of the assessee’s share-dealing business.
The assessee sought to set off the dividend income against business losses brought forward from earlier years.
issues.conclusion: The assessee was entitled to set off the brought-forward business losses against the dividend income from shares held as trading stock.
issues.legal_principle: Section 24(2) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922 concerns carrying forward business losses and setting them off against business profits or gains, rather than limiting set-off by the separate income heads in section 6. Dividends under section 12(1A) form part of business income when received on shares held as trading assets. The Court relied on C.I.T., Andhra Pradesh v. Cocanada Radhaswami Bank Ltd. and referred to Commissioner of Income Tax, Madhya Pradesh v. Shrikishan Chandmal and Commissioner of Income Tax, Ahmedabad v. Bhavnagar Trust Corporation (P.) Ltd.

predicates.tax_assessment_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning the assessment of taxable income.
predicates.business_operated_part_year: The taxpayer carried on business during part of the relevant assessment year.
predicates.brought_forward_business_loss: The taxpayer had a business loss from an earlier year carried forward for set-off.
predicates.dividends_received_on_shares: The taxpayer received dividend income on shares during the relevant year.
predicates.dividend_shares_held_as_trading_stock: The shares producing the dividends formed part of the taxpayer’s trading stock.

issues.definition: In an assessment appeal, a taxpayer that operated a business during part of the year may set off a brought-forward business loss against dividends received on shares held as trading stock.
